text:
Maxim Shabanov's first North American season ended with him leaving the Islanders. Minnesota signed him to a one-year deal in July, and now Hockey Wilderness is arguing the Wild are "leaving production on the table" by not using him more.

They have a point. He has eight goals and 13 points in 20 games, six of the goals in his last ten, and nine of his points on the power play, where he's out for 72% of Minnesota's chances after 27% in New York. His own chances are up to 0.86 expected goals per 60 from 0.62, so the hot streak is built on something real.

The finishing is not going to stay like this. He's scoring on 27% of his shots, three times last season's rate, and still plays only about 15 minutes a night. At five-on-five the Wild are about nine points worse in expected-goal share (the quality of chances) with him than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking likes his puck carrying: a carry-in on 57% of his entries, from only eight tracked games. A power-play winger on a one-year deal, playing for his next one.
